voice.description: A warm adult Indian English narrator, calm and measured, low mid-pitched, reassuring and precise
voice.anchorLine: Drishti is a research and paper trading desk, and this short tour explains how each screen fits together.
voice.style: calm, clear and friendly, explaining to a careful beginner

chapters.title: What Drishti is
lines: Drishti is a research and paper trading desk for Indian equities.
It brings analysis, scanners, plans, risk checks and a simulated ledger into one workflow.
Paper capital is simulated trading money, and analysis credits are a separate balance.
Nothing here promises a profit, and paper results do not prove live execution quality.

chapters.title: The working loop
lines: A session follows one loop.
You set your limits, research a symbol, and write a plan with an entry, a stop and a target.
You size that plan against your risk checks, and you confirm the paper ticket yourself.
Then you read the ledger and the performance screen to see what actually happened.

chapters.title: What stays guarded
lines: Live broker orders sit behind separate gates.
In this deployment live order execution is disabled, so every control you will see is guarded or simulated.

chapters.title: The in-app Guide
lines: The Guide explains each screen where you are standing.
Open it from the top bar, read the help for the current route, or follow a short tour.
Let us walk through the desk.

chapters.title: Start here
lines: Drishti opens on the scanner workbench, and the Guide explains the desk from wherever you are standing.
Paper capital is simulated trading money, and analysis credits are a separate balance that may pay for model analysis.
The order is simple: limits first, then research, a plan, a sizing check, and a paper ticket you confirm deliberately.

chapters.title: Models and connections
lines: Extra provider keys live in Model connections, and the Gemini key is set up in the Analysis form.
Keys are encrypted on the server, and you pick a quick and a deep model in the same analysis form.
OpenAI analysis may use credits, while Gemini and other personal providers run on your own credentials.
The guide never fills in or submits a key for you.

chapters.title: Run and read an analysis
lines: On the Analysis screen you pick a company or ticker, an analysis date, the analysts you want and a research depth.
Review the model choices and the likely usage before you press Run, because you are the one spending credits or provider tokens.
A failed or interrupted run is not a completed recommendation.

chapters.title: Read a report
lines: A run page shows each analyst report, the research debate, and the decision that came out of it.
Check the selected date, the data sources and the status, and use cancel or export where they apply.

chapters.title: Scanners
lines: Scanners let you build rules you can read, and inspect every match with its date and data timestamp.
A match is a research candidate, not a guaranteed trade, and missing bars can stop a rule from being calculated at all.
You decide which candidates move on to research or the watchlist.

chapters.title: Research
lines: Research gathers watchlist news, deals and company results where that data is available.
It explains context, and it never establishes an entry or a fill.
An empty panel can simply mean no matching disclosures, or data that could not be fetched.

chapters.title: Today and watchlist
lines: Today is the working screen: search a symbol, add it to the watchlist, and follow the opening range and entry timer.
Those cards depend on market hours and available bars, so read the waiting reason or the no data note before you act.
Analyse opens the analysis workflow, and it does not confirm a trade.

chapters.title: Plans and exits
lines: A plan records the trade you intend to take: entry, stop rule, target rule and a flat by time.
You can draft one from a symbol and entry, or from a triggered entry timer, and you save your edits before sizing.
Creating a plan does not place an order.

chapters.title: Time Machine
lines: Time Machine compares a plan against historical bars and simulated paths.
Intraday mode needs the entry bar time and at least twenty complete prior session windows.
When the history is not there, the screen reports it honestly: zero full sessions means no test ran, not a test that passed.
Simulated odds are not predictions, and a stop is not a guarantee.

chapters.title: Sizing and risk checks
lines: Sizing turns a saved plan into a reviewable ticket.
It shows quantity, per share risk, total risk, and any check that failed.
Limits cover daily loss, per trade risk, order value, trade count, concentration and required stops.
A blocked ticket needs a corrected plan or a deliberate limit review, never a bypass.

chapters.title: Telegram and messages
lines: Messages connects a Telegram bot to your account, with a verification step you run yourself.
Once updates and paper approvals are enabled, a paper proposal arrives with approve, reject and status controls and a link back to the plan.
Approval is subject to expiry and fresh risk checks, and it only ever applies to a paper proposal.
WhatsApp is optional and needs its own setup.

chapters.title: Paper ledger
lines: The paper ledger is where simulated trades live.
A confirmed ticket waits for an eligible entry bar, and data and price conditions decide whether it fills.
Open and closed trades, exits, charges and net profit and loss are all listed, but a paper fill is not evidence of live execution quality.

chapters.title: Performance
lines: Performance reviews paper outcomes by day and compares what you expected with what happened.
Read the charges, the losses and the sample size, not only the gains.
A new account shows zeros and empty charts, and Drishti leaves them empty rather than filling them in.

chapters.title: Alerts
lines: Alerts are rule based updates you define and then review as triggered events.
Marking an event as seen changes its read status, and nothing about your positions.
Delivery needs a verified channel and enabled preferences, and no alert guarantees a price or an executable entry.

chapters.title: Limits and settings
lines: Limits is the screen that everything else is measured against.
Paper capital, per trade loss, daily loss, maximum order value, concentration, trade counts and time restrictions all live here, and stops are required for entries.
Raising a limit does not make a setup safer, it only moves the line the risk check draws.

chapters.title: Backtests
lines: Evaluation lets you configure a backtest and inspect its status and results.
Running one is a deliberate action that can consume analysis resources.
Historical results depend on the data and the assumptions you chose, and they are not a guarantee that an approach works live.

chapters.title: Zerodha connection
lines: Broker connection uses your own Kite application and your own credentials, stored encrypted.
Daily login is separate from arming, and arming is separate from confirming an order.
Connecting Zerodha does not enable orders, and this deployment keeps live execution disabled.

chapters.title: Strategies and live controls
lines: Finally, Strategies shows the guarded controls: off, paper and confirm modes, connection and data status, daily arming and the kill switch.
Live orders need server enablement, daily arming and explicit per order confirmation, and production live execution is currently disabled.
Paper mode is simulated, and the guide has no action tools, so it never arms a broker or confirms an order.
That is the desk. Open the Guide on any screen for the help that belongs to it, and start with your limits.
